entry.title: How mechanical engineering at Purdue prepared Jessica Traver Ingram to found IntuiTap Medical

media:group.media:title: How mechanical engineering at Purdue prepared Jessica Traver Ingram to found IntuiTap Medical
media:group.media:description:
How can mechanical engineering help an entrepreneur? Jessica Traver Ingram (BSME ’14, MSME ’17) has built her company using the mental fortitude she formed as a Purdue student.
Traver Ingram’s company, IntuiTap Medical, is changing the way patients experience lumbar punctures and diagnostic spinal taps. “If I can make that process better for one person, that’s enough for me,” she says. In 2017, Traver Ingram and her co-founder, Nicole Moskowitz, were named to Forbes’ 30 Under 30 in the healthcare category.
Traver Ingram earned both a bachelor’s and master’s degree in mechanical engineering at Purdue. Mechanical engineers can provide solutions to challenges with energy, the environment, food, housing, water, transportation, safety and health. Common specialty areas are robotics, machine design, sustainable energy and autonomous vehicles. Top industries for mechanical engineering graduates include manufacturing and machinery; airline, aviation and aerospace; automotive; consumer goods and services; and research.
